title: Remapping keys does not work inside the PowerToys itself

status.label: Awaiting the PowerToys feature and operation
status.detail: A maintainer asked where the remapped F14 key is being used; later replies mention a separate elevation concern and a version but do not identify the PowerToys feature.

judgment.rationale: The reporter remaps Caps Lock to F14 and says it is still recognized as Caps Lock inside PowerToys, but does not identify the PowerToys module, command, or operation that should consume F14. A maintainer asked where the key was being used. The reporter's later comments describe a separate elevated-app launch concern and state a version, but do not answer that question. Keep the existing request rather than posting a duplicate or claiming a fix path.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.88.0 and Keyboard Manager and describes remapping Caps Lock to F14 for use inside PowerToys.
A maintainer asked on 2025-01-31 where the remapped key was being used because the target was unclear.
The reporter later described an elevated-app launch concern and said the problem occurred on version 0.91.1, but did not identify the PowerToys feature or operation using F14.

Issues #35644, #35844, and #36347 were closed as duplicates of #36193, which concerns broader remapping failures; that does not establish the same scope as using remapped input within a PowerToys feature.
The issue remains open without an assignee.
judgment.recommended_action: Await the exact PowerToys feature and operation that should receive F14, then assess whether the remapped input is intentionally ignored or incorrectly handled by that consumer.
judgment.requested_evidence: Identify the specific PowerToys feature and operation where Caps Lock remapped to F14 is still recognized as Caps Lock, as requested in the maintainer comment https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/37183#issuecomment-2626971062.

fix_assessment.rationale: Without knowing which PowerToys component should consume the remapped input, there is no specific event path or expected behavior against which to justify a code change. The issue remains open for clarification rather than being dismissed.
